gloss: Carries two accounts of Badr: Umar's, of the Prophet's supplication for help before the angels arrived, and Ibn Abbas's, of the deliberation afterwards over what should be done with the captives.

gloss: Reports that during the fighting the Prophet took up a handful of dust and flung it toward the ranks of the Quraysh, with the words that their faces be scorched.

A companion was suspected of sending word to the Quraysh, and permission was sought to strike his neck. The Prophet refused it, on the ground that the man had been present at Badr and that the people of Badr already stood forgiven.
Names the six men who fought the single combat that opened the battle, three from each side, and identifies them as the ones concerning whom 22:19 was revealed.
Puts the Muslim fighters at Badr at a little over three hundred and ten, and sets that number explicitly beside the number of those who crossed the river with Talut in the Qur'anic account.
Reports the Prophet marking out in advance the places where four of the Quraysh leaders would fall, and a companion's confirmation afterwards that each was found dead at the spot named for him.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's own account: he took a sword from what was captured at Badr and asked to keep it, was told to put it back, and was granted it only after the ruling on the spoils came down.

Miqdad's declaration before the battle that the Muslims would not hold back as the Israelites had told Musa to do, but would fight at the Prophet's side. The Prophet's face is described as showing his pleasure at the words.

Umayr ibn al-Humam, hearing that paradise is as wide as the heavens and the earth, threw away the dates still in his hand as too long a thing to wait for, went forward into the fighting, and was killed.
